pamphlet_excerpts: Raised Ink Surfaces: Relief printing uses a raised surface to press ink onto paper (p. 17).
Letterpress and Flexography: The most common forms of relief printing are letterpress and flexography (p. 17).
Movable Type Origins: Letter press is one of the oldest printing methods, with its origins in the movable type invented in China in the 11th century and in Germany (p. 17).
Reusable Metal Type: The significance of Johann Gutenberg's invention was that his movable metal type was reusable (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Letterpress Origins: Letter press is one of the oldest printing methods, with its origins in the movable type invented in China in the 11th century and in Germany (p. 17).
Step 2 - Examine Metal Type: The significance of Johann Gutenberg's invention was that his movable metal type was reusable (p. 17).
Step 3 - Set Reusable Type: Individual letters could be set by hand for a printing job, printed, and then taken apart and used in another project (p. 17).
Step 4 - Compare Modern Methods: Letter press printing was the dominant process for 500 years, but new technologies in the last 50 years have offered better and more efficient ways (p. 17).

quiz_item.question: In Graphic Arts Requirement 1, how do the four traditional printing processes (relief, intaglio, planographic, and porous) transfer ink to a substrate?
options: A. All four processes carve deep grooves into wooden blocks and melt solid wax crayons onto the paper using laser beams.
B. Offset lithography forces ink through a woven silk mesh, while screen printing etches microscopic wells into a heavy copper cylinder.

C. Relief prints from raised surfaces, gravure/intaglio prints from recessed ink-filled cells etched into a cylinder, offset lithography prints from a flat plate using the mutual repulsion of oil-based ink and water, and screen printing squeegees ink through open mesh areas of a stencil.
D. Gravure uses raised rubber stamps for corrugated cardboard, while flexography uses only home inkjet cartridges.

pamphlet_excerpts: Microscopic Halftone Dots: The half tone dots are so small, the human eye cannot see the individual dots unless they are magnified, but the eye does see an overall effect (p. 44).
Optical Tone Illusion: The arrangement of the half tone dots creates this effect (p. 44).
Shadow Dot Density: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look dark are big and fill most of the half tone dot area (p. 44).
Highlight Dot Spacing: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look light are small and fill very little of the halftone dot area (p. 44).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Inspect Shadow Dots: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look dark are big and fill most of the half tone dot area (p. 44).
Step 2 - Inspect Highlight Dots: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look light are small and fill very little of the halftone dot area (p. 44).
Step 3 - Select Continuous-Tone Photo: Generally, half tones are made from a continuous-tone image, such as a traditional photograph (p. 44).
Step 4 - Convert Image to Halftone: In the past, the continuous-tone image was photographed through a special screen that created a half tone version of the original (p. 44).

quiz_item.question: How does a single color of black ink on a printing press create the appearance of dark shadows and bright highlights in a halftone photograph?
options: A. The press applies thicker layers of wet ink in dark areas and thinner layers in light areas
B. Dark areas use large dots that fill most of the grid while light areas use tiny dots
C. White ink is mixed into the fountain rollers to lighten the highlight regions
D. The paper is chemically bleached after printing to fade the highlight sections
choices: A. The press applies thicker layers of wet ink in dark areas and thinner layers in light areas
B. Dark areas use large dots that fill most of the grid while light areas use tiny dots
C. White ink is mixed into the fountain rollers to lighten the highlight regions
D. The paper is chemically bleached after printing to fade the highlight sections
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Dark areas use large dots that fill most of the grid while light areas use tiny dots
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Halftones simulate continuous shading by varying dot size: large dots fill dark shadow areas while small dots leave mostly white paper showing in light areas (p. 44).

B. Offset lithography forces ink through a woven silk mesh, while screen printing etches microscopic wells into a heavy copper cylinder.

C. Relief prints from raised surfaces, gravure/intaglio prints from recessed ink-filled cells etched into a cylinder, offset lithography prints from a flat plate using the mutual repulsion of oil-based ink and water, and screen printing squeegees ink through open mesh areas of a stencil.
D. Gravure uses raised rubber stamps for corrugated cardboard, while flexography uses only home inkjet cartridges.
choices: A. All four processes carve deep grooves into wooden blocks and melt solid wax crayons onto the paper using laser beams.
